claims: A total lunar eclipse occurred early on March 3, 2026.
The March 3, 2026 total lunar eclipse was visible over North America, Asia, Australia, and the Pacific.
The next total lunar eclipse after March 3, 2026 will not happen until December 31, 2028.
The next total lunar eclipse date is December 31, 2028 - January 1, 2029.
A total lunar eclipse occurs when Earth passes directly between the Sun and Moon.
A blood moon occurs during a total lunar eclipse when Earth aligns between the Sun and the Moon, blocking direct sunlight.
Earth's atmosphere scatters sunlight, with red light refracted onto the Moon's surface and blue light scattered away during a blood moon.
The totality during a blood moon usually lasts around 75 minutes to over an hour.
A blood moon is safe to view directly with the naked eye.
A blood moon does not require special filters or telescopes.
The March 3, 2026 total lunar eclipse was visible in North America, Asia, and Australia.
The March 3, 2026 total lunar eclipse marked the first of the year.
Total lunar eclipses took place in March 2025 and September 2025
